Maintenance Report — MNT-0150-002

Asset: WELL-0150 (NE-07 Well 150, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: rod string Work started: 10 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 20 Dec 2022 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 240 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0150-0008 on 2022-12-08 Report written: 21 Dec 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0150-0008 showed the wellhead at 20.9 °C with the air at 12.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods6,548
Rod couplings1,637
Fishing tool rental2,728
Labour (company crew)5,790
Total16,703

Compliance check

WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0150-007

Asset: WELL-0150 (NE-07 Well 150, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 11 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 Aug 2023 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0150-0043 on 2023-08-10 Report written: 13 Aug 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0150-0043 at 10:30 on 2023-08-10 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.6% of the pad area, estimated 1.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 7.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 361 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 289 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.0 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0150-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.25% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0150-017

Asset: WELL-0150 (NE-07 Well 150, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 02 Apr 2025 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 599 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0150-0125 on 2025-03-06 Report written: 03 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0150-0125 showed the wellhead at 19.7 °C with the air at 15.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
